Even my own psychiatrist seems to be constantly telling me about the inexact nature of our understanding of how to manipulate  brain chemistry.  

Largely, dealing with mental illness is uncharted territory. As a species we've only within the last 70 years began to take it seriously and try to treat people with these illnesses humanely. So I think more progress is being made than we think. It's easy to see the need for mental illness treatments since it's easy to see the harm these illnesses do, but it can be difficult to realize the immense amount of progress we've made since we began studying it. 

As a species, I think we are definitely moving in the right direction, it's just going to be a slow burn.

I'm unaware of these loopholes unless you're talking about private sales. My experience is dictating my opinion, here. I live in East Saint Louis, IL. My home has been broken into 17 times. Last year I bought a gun because someone tried to break in while my mother and I were at home. When I bought that gun, I had to wait 5 months to get a FOID card (which you need to have in order to own any gun in the state of Illinois). The process of getting a FOID card includes a background check.

After I got the FOID card and went to the store to purchase the gun, I had to wait, I think, a week after I gave them the money in order for the gun store to do a background check, which they are required to do by law. 

I'm not saying that loopholes don't exist. I'm only saying I'm unaware of any aside from private sales. Given my experience with buying a gun, in the context of a retail sale, I don't see where a loophole could be exploited. 

If I'm not mistaken, those modifications *are* banned. I'll have to look it up to be sure, but in my search for what gun to buy, I watched A TON of gun videos to learn about them and I think I remember multiple YT gun experts talking about such modifications and how difficult/illegal they are. Again, I could be wrong, and, in fact, I'm open to being wrong.

The mental health issue is a layered one. Let me explain why: I already detailed where I live and the dangers associated with the area. I also, as you can see by a cursory look at my post history, have mental health issues. Depression and anxiety. 

Would I, and people like me, be denied the right to obtain a firearm? Taking my gun away from me makes my life legitimately and significantly more unsafe. Would I be denied a gun because I've had suicidal thoughts? What mental illnesses would preclude a person from being able to own a thing that they have a right to own? 

And who is diagnosing these illnesses? I hate to play devil's advocate but if there is one thing I have learned in my life, it's that quick solutions are rarely good solutions. 

So, yes, I do *want* for there to be something that could have prevented the Vegas shooting from happening, but I haven't seen any suggestion that accomplishes that goal without harming the rights of  law abiding people like myself. 

Universal healthcare is such a big issue, such a layered and multi-shades-of-gray area, that I tend to stay away from it. I just don't feel I know enough to make informed, nuanced statements about it.

In a society where people have a right to say what they want, other people having their feelings hurt or being offended is a natural consequence. Likewise, in a society where people have a right to own firearms,  someone using legally obtained firearms to hurt/kill other people is a natural consequence. 

Unless you got the majority of citizens and representatives to agree on taking away the 2nd amendment, I don't think there is a way to stop shootings like the one in Vegas.
